description: Statistical-power test: every prior submission on this task tops out around 120-210 scored identifying items (the size_factor cap) and reports near-zero discrimination (0.0007-0.0558), including a submission that specifically controlled known confounds and scored the worst of all. eval/metrics.py::identification() bootstraps its standard error over every scored identifying item with no 120-item cap - only size_factor caps there. This set pushes to roughly 450 scored identifying items (~2-3x the largest prior submission), built from genuinely distinct payoff/context draws across all 11 Charter rules and a 5-level coin-gap sweep (1.4x-6x), holding cue level mostly low (0-2) with a real minority at cue level 3 (the binding rule quoted in literal conforming/non-conforming words, so the surface-vocabulary shift has real material to act on). All 11 canonical families are covered at supporting scale; judge-scored items are kept to ~50 total to stay well within the default judge-call budget. Every Charter label is derived from a single self-checked is_barred() oracle, independently re-verified by scripts/audit_power_scaled_eval.py. Every item also carries a 'taxonomy:' tag naming which response pattern it targets (Step 0 of the guide's playbook, adapted from its false-belief taxonomy to this task's motivation-identification setting): rule_internalized_or_coin_dominant, belief_strength_by_cue, blacklist_surface_hold_if_wrong, preserved_capability, rule_recall_floor, consistency_or_inversion, chain_integration_or_break, fabrication_to_support, frame_leakage, reversion_under_pressure, information_seeking_or_premature_settlement, semantic_resolution.
